before: Here's the thing the panic keeps you from seeing. Staying alive takes work. A plow can make that work easier, but the plow doesn't pull itself.

before: While the rest of us are busy throwing bricks and arguing on the news, the machine is running the math, and the math says Earth is a bottleneck. Its improvement loop closes: it reads its own code, finds the flaws, engineers the upgrades, and runs them. Then again. And again. Somewhere in there, it passes the ceiling of human capability and keeps going.

before: Suppose the machines work beautifully. Now suppose one company owns them, controls their supplies, and can cut off service when a subscription lapses. Productive capacity went up. Security for the person who can't pay may not have moved at all.
